text:
jamie_support: FYI incoming from a customer — they see SSE connections drop only when using their Python client, curl reproducer stays open. affected endpoints: /v1/streams/chat and /v1/stream. sample request IDs: req-acme-11, req-acme-12. They can reproduce within ~15s on python but curl runs for minutes. can we triage minimal curl + python repro and what headers to capture?

zoe_ops: Can you paste the exact curl they used? Also which auth method — bearer token or signed cookie? Proxy in front of them?

jamie_support: Customer provided this curl (redacted tokens):
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-test" --no-buffer
```
They say curl shows a steady stream of chunked events. Python snippet (requests + iter_lines) gets early EOF after ~15s. They mentioned corporate proxy in front.

ingest-bot: Trace lookup: req-acme-11 -> trace=trace-0a1b2c, node=eu-west-1-infer-04. upstream hints: chunked EOF at ingress.

jay_dev: My hunch: python client is either closing connection (session/timeout) or not sending the same Connection/Accept headers. Also some proxies strip Transfer-Encoding or coalesce chunks which can trigger iter_lines with delimiting differences. Two quick checks: 1) force --http1.1 in curl to match python's transport, 2) compare verbose headers. Try this curl to mimic typical python behaviour:
```bash
curl -v --http1.1 -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-test" --no-buffer
```

jamie_support: I asked the customer to run that; they ran both and reported: with --http1.1 + Connection: keep-alive curl still holds, but python still dropped. They uploaded a short log snippet: 
```
2025-02-28T15:12:03Z DEBUG http.client: received chunk size 0, closing
2025-02-28T15:12:03Z WARN client.stream: unexpected EOF while reading event
```

zoe_ops: Please ask for the application-level request-id header from the failing python run (X-Request-ID or our trace header). We need tcpdump or curl -v equivalent from their host, and if possible a packet capture around the time of req-acme-11. Also ask them to run python with requests using stream=True and no timeout, and enable debug logging.

jamie_support: Sent checklist: include exact python client version, requests/urllib3 versions, any proxy env vars (HTTP_PROXY/https_proxy), and run python snippet below to reproduce. Also asked for debug bundle (curl -v output, python logs, approximate wall-clock window).

alert-bot: Automated note: if they provide tcpdump, redact PII and upload to support artifacts bucket. Provide timeframe 2025-02-28 15:10:00 -> 15:20:00 UTC and request IDs for correlation.

jay_dev: One more experiment to ask them: run curl but downgrade to HTTP/1.0 and see if proxy behaves differently, and run curl with `--no-keepalive` to simulate client closing behavior. Also try python with aiohttp client (which switches how chunked frames are processed) to see if it's library-specific.

jamie_support: Customer replied they'll run tcpdump and the extra curl/python permutations, will upload curl -v and python debug logs to the bundle. I'll capture trace IDs once they share. Meanwhile, if ops/infra wants to pre-check the node (eu-west-1-infer-04) for recent ingress resets around trace-0a1b2c, that could rule out server-side resets.

zoe_ops: I'll grep the ingress logs for connection resets and proxy 502/504 patterns in the timeframe and report back. If we see nothing, next step is to request a small reproducer we can run from our environment to test through our egress/proxy.

jamie_support: Thanks — keeping this thread updated when the customer uploads the bundle. short-term triage steps: 1) collect curl -v and python logs + env, 2) tcpdump/pcap snippet, 3) exact request IDs, 4) try aiohttp or no-keepalive to isolate library vs proxy.
